edges.component: CMOS image sensors (iPhone camera sensors)
edges.basis: Apple has confirmed that Sony supplies iPhone camera sensors (Tim Cook, Dec 2022), but neither Apple nor Sony gives a share. Sony's 20-F for the fiscal year ended 2026-03-31 (filed 2026-06-18) never mentions 'Apple' and gives no customer-concentration figure. So the size can only come from wording in reputable outlets: Sony is the 'sole supplier' of iPhone image sensors (MacRumors, Dec 2025), Apple has 'relied exclusively on Sony' (TrendForce, Aug 2025), and Apple 'sourced all image sensors for its iPhones from Japan's Sony' (Korea Herald, Aug 2025). In Sept 2025 Ming-Chi Kuo said Samsung's iPhone CIS mass volume had probably slipped to 2027, and that Samsung's ultrawide CIS would go into mid- to low-end iPhones first. The line 'For now, Sony will continue to be Apple's exclusive camera sensor supplier' is from Wccftech's own author (Omar Sohail), not Kuo. In Feb 2026, Y.M.Cinema, citing Nikkei Business, said Samsung supply was expected 'as early as 2027'. The rule maps 'sole / exclusive / only supplier' to 0.95. No outlet gives a percentage, so this is QUALITATIVE, not REPORTED. Contrary signal, not relied on: after the June 2026 Tata Electronics data leak, lower-tier outlets (Sammy Fans, 2026-07-03; SoftwareSeni) said Samsung appears as an image-sensor supplier in the iPhone 18 Pro supplier map ('a slice has been cut and given to Samsung'). MacRumors, 9to5Mac, Al Jazeera and Outlook Business covered the leak but none of them named camera-sensor suppliers. TechInsights' iPhone 18 Pro Max teardown (2026-09-18) still lists camera sensors as analysis in progress. If a reputable teardown shows a Samsung sensor in a shipping iPhone, re-map this to 'primary' = 0.70.
edges.as_of: 2026 (Sony still described as the sole or exclusive iPhone image-sensor supplier. Reputable reporting puts Samsung's Austin-made sensors at 2027 mass volume, starting with the ultrawide sensor in lower-end iPhones. Expect this to fall to 0.70 under the 'primary' rule once Samsung ships.)
edges.notes:
The relationship is certain: Apple's CEO has confirmed it publicly. The size is less certain, because it rests only on wording in the press ('sole' / 'exclusive' / 'all'). Neither company discloses a share. Sony's 2026 20-F has no mention of Apple and no figures on how concentrated its customers are. The invented 0.81 should be replaced with 0.95.

This figure will go down. Apple's 6 Aug 2025 release announced chips from Samsung's Austin fab. Apple did not say they are image sensors; outlets (TrendForce, FT via Engadget/MacRumors, Kuo, Nikkei Business) report they are stacked iPhone image sensors. Kuo says the first ones are 48MP ultra-wide sensors for lower- and mid-range iPhones, with mass volume in 2027. MacRumors expects them first in the base iPhone 18 in the first half of 2027. After that, Sony would become 'primary' rather than 'sole' (0.70 under the rule) once a source confirms it.

No source confirms the suppliers in the iPhone 18 Pro (launched Sept 2026) yet. The iFixit teardown (2026-09-20) names no sensor maker. The TechInsights preliminary teardown (2026-09-18) lists camera sensors as 'Analysis in progress'. Pre-launch leaks naming a Sony IMX905 were not treated as evidence.

Pages I could not open myself: the Tim Cook tweet on x.com (HTTP 402), so its text was checked through The Daily Star; the TechInsights article 'Sony Keeps Lead in Apple's iPhone Image Sensors' (paywalled, no content returned); and the original FT and Nikkei Business articles, which I saw only through secondary outlets.

The 'sole supplier' wording covers the iPhone's camera image sensors. I did not check the Face ID / TrueDepth infrared sensors.

edges.component: LFP cells (Megapack, Shanghai-built Model 3/Y)
edges.basis: No reputable source gives a percentage for CATL's share of Tesla's LFP cells. Tesla's FY2025 10-K names CATL as a cell supplier for both vehicles and energy storage. LatePost, via CnEVPost, calls CATL the "primary supplier" of cells for the Shanghai Megafactory and says CATL "remains the largest supplier" to Tesla's energy storage business. Under the mapping rule, primary/main maps to 0.70. The same report gives BYD's FinDreams "more than 20 percent" of Shanghai Megafactory supply, so CATL's share there is below about 80%, which fits 0.70. ETNews says CATL supplies the entire volume of Tesla's prismatic EV cells, which alone would map to 0.95. That claim covers vehicles only, and reports of BYD cells at Giga Berlin conflict with it. CATL's position is shrinking, but no newer source shows a change in its rank. Tesla stopped using Chinese LFP cells in US-built cars after 2024. Tesla's own Nevada LFP line is only 7 GWh and in early ramp (Q2 2026), against 46.7 GWh of storage deployed in 2025. LG Energy Solution's US LFP supply does not start until August 2027. The claim that energy storage is Tesla's largest LFP use is an inference and is not directly sourced.
edges.as_of: Ranking evidence: LatePost via CnEVPost, 2024-06-05 and 2024-12-26. Relationship still confirmed in Tesla FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-01-29) and WSJ via Just Auto (2025-11-17). No source found that is newer than Dec 2024 and changes CATL's rank.
edges.notes:
Scope: LFP cells: prismatic LFP for Megapack (mainly Shanghai Megafactory and US energy storage) and Shanghai-built Model 3/Y Standard/RWD. US-built Tesla cars no longer use CATL/Chinese LFP cells (WSJ via Just Auto, 2025-11-17).

The relationship is real and current. Tesla's FY2025 10-K names CATL, and CATL's supply contract with Tesla was extended to 2025 (S&P AutoTechInsight citing Reuters, 2021-06-29). What is not public is a numeric share of Tesla's LFP cells. Figures I checked and rejected: (1) Adamas Intelligence via ETNews (2022-02-20) put CATL at 18.5 GWh of Tesla's 2021 EV cells, about 28% of the ~65 GWh total, but that covers all chemistries, EVs only, and is stale. (2) A claim that Tesla committed to 20 GWh of CATL cells for 2026-2028, 'about 30%' of Tesla Energy's needs, appears only on low-quality blogs (teslaacessories.com, optimusk.blog) with no primary source, so I excluded it. (3) InsideEVs' 'remaining 80% likely CATL' for the Shanghai Megafactory is the outlet's own inference. CATL's share is falling: BYD FinDreams won 'more than 20 percent' of Shanghai Megafactory orders (LatePost, 2024), EVE Energy was added as a storage supplier (2024-12), and Tesla's own Nevada LFP line is in early ramp (7 GWh installed). LG Energy Solution's $4.3B Michigan LFP contract starts August 2027. Reuters (2025-07-30) quotes Tesla's CFO saying tariffs hit the energy business 'since it sources LFP batteries from China'. The ETNews quotes came through a summarizing fetch; the Korean wording was returned verbatim, but I did not see the full page. The Bloomberg (2026-04-22) and TheStreet pages returned 403 and I did not use them. Consider cutting to 0.50 if the app wants to reflect the 2026-2027 diversification, but no source currently supports a lower figure.

edges.component: Foundry wafers (one of three primary foundries)
edges.basis: Qualcomm's FY2025 10-K (period ended 2025-09-28, filed 2025-11-05) names Samsung as one of three primary foundry suppliers, alongside TSMC and GlobalFoundries, and gives no share. Under the rule, 'one of several / a supplier' maps to 0.25. No filing, outlet or analyst publishes a numeric Samsung share of Qualcomm wafers. At Snapdragon Summit on 2026-09-22, Qualcomm SVP Chris Patrick said all of the newly announced 2nm parts are made by TSMC. edges.as_of: FY2025 10-K (filed 2025-11-05); flagship foundry status as of 2026-09-22 (Snapdragon Summit)
edges.notes:
Scope: Foundry wafers for Qualcomm chips. Samsung is one of three named primary foundries. Qualcomm confirmed that its flagship 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 are both made by TSMC, so the 'dual-source' label is not supported

The claimed 0.39 is unsupported. The relationship itself is disclosed in the 10-K, but that disclosure covers all Qualcomm ICs, not Snapdragon SoCs specifically. Snapdragon premium SoCs have been TSMC-only since Qualcomm moved the 8 Gen 1 family to TSMC in 2022. The 2026 flagships (8 Elite Gen 5, including the 'for Galaxy' variant, plus 8 Elite Gen 6 and Extreme Gen 6) are all TSMC. A Samsung-made 2nm 'Kaanapali S' / 8 Elite Gen 5 was reported in 2025 and Jan 2026, but TrendForce (Sept 2026) says Qualcomm AP production at Samsung 2nm has not started. The rule-mapped 0.25 therefore probably overstates Samsung's share of Snapdragon SoC wafers, and no public number exists to refine it. Recommendation: rename the component as shown and drop the 'dual-source' wording. If the app needs strictly the 'Snapdragon SoC' edge, set keep=false as unsourced at the product level. The Sammy Fans page is a secondary report of the Qualcomm executive's remarks; the Chosun/Korean original was not opened. The Qualcomm press release page for the 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy could not be read (fetch timed out) and is not relied on.

edges.component: 4N/4NP (Blackwell) and 3nm (Rubin) GPU dies
edges.basis: No filing or analyst gives a numeric share. NVIDIA's 10-K names 'foundries, such as TSMC and Samsung' for all of its wafers, which is company-wide and not specific to GPU dies. For this component, NVIDIA's own statements tie the dies to TSMC. Blackwell GPUs are 'manufactured using a custom-built TSMC 4NP process', which is TSMC's own process, so no other foundry can make those dies. For Rubin, CEO Jensen Huang said all six new chips (CPU, GPU, NVLink switch, networking chip, networking switch, silicon photonics) were taped out to TSMC: 'All these new chips are now in TSMC's fab.' 'All ... in TSMC's fab' is read as sole/only supplier, which maps to 0.95. Caveat: the rule's literal keywords (sole/exclusive/only) do not appear in any NVIDIA source. TrendForce (Jun 2026) calls TSMC NVIDIA's 'primary' partner, but that describes the whole company, not this component. Against: NVIDIA is only testing Intel 18A (evaluation/MPW stage, no production order), and the Samsung 4nm part in Vera Rubin is Groq's LPX/LP30, not an NVIDIA GPU die.

In June 2026, President Trump said Apple agreed to build chips with Intel. The WSJ, via MacRumors (Jul 2026), reports that Apple plans Intel-made chips for Mac laptops and iPhones but gives no timeline. ITS iPHONE FOOTPRINT HAS SHRUNK A LOT:
(1) Kunshan (Jiangsu): 62.5% sold to Luxshare in Dec 2023. On 2025-08-13 Pegatron's board approved selling its remaining shares of Luxsan Precision Industry (Kunshan) (2025 Annual Report).

Output from that plant belongs to Tata, not Pegatron.
(3) Shanghai: the only large Pegatron-controlled iPhone site confirmed by sources (Bloomberg via AppleInsider, 2023). Its current iPhone volume is not disclosed.
The India share figures below no longer describe Pegatron and should not be used: Counterpoint (Sep 2023) put Pegatron at about 10% of India iPhone output, and Bloomberg via TrendForce (Apr 2024) put it at about 17% of India output for the prior year.

Its two-year forecast of global iPhone assembly share is Foxconn 55-60%, Luxshare 30% and Tata 10-15%. Those add up to 95-105%, and Pegatron is not named at all. That implies Pegatron's own share is about 0-5%. This is my arithmetic, not a figure any source reports. If the app wants a number that matches the evidence rather than the wording rule, the defensible options are: (a) cap the edge at about 0.05 and label it as a residual derived from Bloomberg Intelligence, or (b) set it to null until an analyst publishes a figure for Pegatron.
